book.title: The New Penguin Book of The Guardian Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Horsy type needed to demonstrate knitwear

parts.note: to show is to demonstrate
a jumper is a knitted pullover, a sweater

explanation.surface: Someone with equestrian tastes must model a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A showjumper is a horse or rider competing over fences in an arena event.

clue.text: Article those people in motoring body find an object of abhorrence

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the people go in the middle of the motoring body's letters

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, Britain's motoring organisation
them means those people

explanation.surface: Members of a motoring club regard some item with disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is something detested or loathed, originally a thing cursed by the church.

clue.text: Assume control in order to act as executor?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words
second meaning: an executioner ..., executing the condemned

explanation.walkthrough: Split as BE HEAD it means take charge; whole, it is what an executioner does, and the question mark flags 'executor' as one who executes rather than a will's administrator.
explanation.definitionFit: To behead is to cut off someone's head, the job of an executioner at an execution.

clue.text: Bulk service

definitions.meaning: first meaning: size, volume, weight
second meaning: the Eucharist church service

explanation.definitionFit: The word means quantity of matter or a large amount, and also the Catholic celebration of the Eucharist.

clue.text: Made a proclamation marked with emphasis

definitions.meaning: first meaning: declared formally
second meaning: very noticeable, strongly marked

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means declared or announced officially; as an adjective, conspicuous or decided.

clue.text: Cheat got an alteration in Stock Exchange term

parts.note: to con is to cheat or swindle

indicators.note: an alteration changes something, here the order of the letters

explanation.surface: A swindler obtains a change in the wording of a market rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Contango was the charge paid on the old London exchange for deferring settlement of a purchase of shares.

clue.text: Part of meal at sporting venue

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one dish in a sequence, such as the main
second meaning: a racecourse or golf ...

explanation.definitionFit: A dinner has several dishes served in turn, and races and golf are held over a laid-out ground.

clue.text: Treat wood

definitions.meaning: first meaning
second meaning: pine or fir timber

explanation.definitionFit: To deal with someone is to handle them; deal is also softwood timber such as pine planks.

clue.text: Barbarian man bearing fugitive appearance

parts.note: the Huns were the archetypal barbarian invaders
Ted is a man's name
one's bearing is one's air or manner

explanation.surface: A savage warrior carries himself with the look of someone on the run.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunted air is the haunted, furtive look of someone being pursued, as a fugitive would wear.

clue.text: Weight one put on in seaside air

indicators.note: one is placed after, as if put on to the end of, the weight

parts.note: oz is the abbreviation for ounce, a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone gains weight on holiday by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is the popular name for the bracing fresh air of the coast, thought to be invigorating.

clue.text: Part of horse that becomes dry

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ridge between a horse's shoulder blades
second meaning: shrivels and dries up, as a plant does

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the high point of a horse's back by the neck; the verb describes a plant drying and shrivelling.

clue.text: Note that is without affectation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in music, a note that is neither sharp nor flat
second meaning: unaffected, unpretentious

explanation.definitionFit: In music a natural is a note restored from sharp or flat; a natural manner is unforced and genuine.

clue.text: Turn head-over-heels in high finish

parts.note: up means high, aloft
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A gymnast completes a routine with a lofty somersault.
explanation.definitionFit: To up-end something is to turn it upside down, tipping it over so its bottom is uppermost.

clue.text: Reject with scorn teacher of prominence in Yorkshire?

parts.note: to spurn is to reject contemptuously
the head is the head teacher of a school

explanation.surface: A haughty schoolmaster brushes someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurn Head is a long sand-spit headland at the mouth of the Humber in East Yorkshire; 'prominence' means a jutting landform, not fame.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland is a promontory, a piece of land jutting out, and this one lies on the Yorkshire coast.

clue.text: Purely accidental success landing very thin fish

parts.note: sheer fabric is very fine, almost transparent
a fluke is a flatfish, a flounder

explanation.surface: An angler happens to bring in a skinny catch by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluke is a lucky stroke, and sheer stresses it was due to nothing but chance.

clue.text: Private-sector laundry work?

parts.note: the soiled washing one keeps out of public view stands for private scandals

explanation.walkthrough: 'Private-sector' sounds like business, but it means one's private affairs; the idiom is to wash such things in public.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names embarrassing personal matters, from the image of soiled household washing kept indoors.

clue.text: Plain glass found in covered wagon

parts.note: a prairie is a vast grassy plain
a schooner is a large drinking glass, for sherry or beer

explanation.surface: An ordinary drinking glass turns up inside a pioneer's cart.
explanation.definitionFit: The canvas-topped wagons used by American settlers crossing the plains were nicknamed after sailing ships.

clue.text: Goes back over misfortunes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: retraces, goes backwards
second meaning: setbacks, defeats

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means turns back or retraces; as a plural noun, setbacks or reversals of fortune.

clue.text: Left in Red Sea, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone was abandoned in the Red Sea, possibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like abandoned, but it is the side of a road vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the nearside of a car is the kerb side, which is the left-hand side.

clue.text: Got back into highly thought-of company

indicators.note: the company abbreviation goes into the middle of the other word

parts.note: revered means greatly respected

explanation.surface: Someone regains a place among a respected set of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovered means retrieved or regained something that was lost.

clue.text: The craft of a tailor

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small sailing vessel
second meaning: the person who cuts the cloth in a tailor's shop

explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' reads as a skill, but it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutter is a single-masted boat, and also the tailor who cuts out garments.

clue.text: Small book about artist in do-it-yourself

indicators.note: in places the turned artist inside the home-improvement letters
about means turned about, so the artist's letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A slim manual for home improvement contains material on a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RA into AR, which goes 'in' DIY.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary is a little book for recording appointments or daily events.

clue.text: Meaningless scrawl of party on dole, perhaps

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters in another possible order

explanation.surface: Someone out of work scribbles at a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges DOLE into ODLE; the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A doodle is an aimless drawing made absent-mindedly.

clue.text: Misprint that is not metaphorical

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a printer's term for a typographical error
second meaning: taking words in their exact sense

explanation.definitionFit: Printers call a typo a literal; as an adjective it means exact rather than figurative.

clue.text: Run right out of petrol?

indicators.note: out of says the right letters leave the fuel word and what remains is jumbled

explanation.surface: A motorist has to run because the tank is quite empty.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R and T (right) from PETROL, leaving PEOL, and the question mark licenses rearranging it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long easy bounding strides.

clue.text: Oriental pilots guided round Romanian oil town

indicators.note: the letters are steered round into a new order

parts.note: E for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: Eastern aviators are escorted round a refinery town in Romania.
explanation.walkthrough: PLOESTI, now usually spelt Ploiești, was the centre of Romania's oil industry.
explanation.definitionFit: The city north of Bucharest was a famous petroleum-refining centre, bombed heavily in the Second World War.

clue.text: The vessel for Irish money

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flat-bottomed boat
second meaning: the Irish pound before the euro

explanation.definitionFit: A punt is a long boat pushed with a pole, and was also the name of Ireland's pound currency.

clue.text: A bit of something to eat at church

parts.note: a pie is food
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A snack served at a church gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion or fragment of something larger.

clue.text: County were first to reject, for example, pig-iron for ships' ballast

parts.note: Kent is an English county
those who led were at the front

indicators.note: to reject something is to turn it back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: EG abbreviates the Latin exempli gratia

explanation.surface: A county team led the way in turning down an offer of scrap metal for ballast.
explanation.definitionFit: Kentledge is the term for pig-iron blocks laid in a ship's hold as permanent weight.
